answer: Each identity posts a 50-credit bond in the hollow ledger; each action draws down that bond. The cedar auditors record every action: the first 10 in an epoch cost 1 credit each, the next 20 cost 2 each, and any beyond 30 costs 5 each. The k-th fake identity thus costs 50 in bond plus 50 in drawdown for 30 actions, and 1,000 fakes cost 100,000 credits, with no sharing across identities. An action-splitting ring fails: each fresh identity adds a new 50 bond, and identities below 10 actions earn no weight. The saffron audit burns any replayed bond. An honest identity pays 50 plus 50 drawdown.
